body.statement: Suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  There are constants \(c_0>0\) and \(\eta_0>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the base Holder model class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws whose realized interior paths are separated by order \(N^{-1/2}\), whose observed-data total variation distance is at most \(1-\eta_0\), and whose causal targets are separated by at least \(c_0N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The training and treated-event observed laws can be chosen identical; only the donor-location experiment and the transported untreated potential mean differ.  No lower local-modulus condition is used.
body.justification: A common-support three-point location family and an affine or cusp regression directly certify the donor lower rate without a class-wide modulus.
body.gap: At the Jensen-minimal fourth-moment boundary the donor law may be singular, so strict moment slack is genuinely required.
body.consumer: The marginal MSE and honest-length converses use this regular overlapping family.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  We first construct a regular donor location family satisfying the full covariance and fourth-moment restrictions.  Choose \(a_D>1\) so that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) sufficiently small, put a variable \(V_u\) on \(\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) with probabilities
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
At \(u=0\) all three probabilities are strictly positive, so they remain positive on a fixed neighborhood of zero.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E V_u=u,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Let the remaining \(q-1\) standardized donor coordinates be independent Rademacher variables.  At \(u=0\), independence and (1) give
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =q(q-1)+(q-1)+a_D^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.
\tag{4}
\]
The left side with centering at the mean \(u\) is a continuous polynomial in \(u\) and the probabilities (2); consequently it remains below \(B^4\) for all sufficiently small \(|u|\).

Set \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and \(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where \(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Because \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths obey the interior restriction for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under law \(v\in\{0,1\}\), take the first donor coordinate to be \(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\), take the other coordinates to be \(1/2\) plus the common Rademacher coordinates, and make donors i.i.d.  Equations (3)--(4) show that
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,\qquad
 \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.
\tag{5}
\]
Since \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), (5) verifies full covariance ellipticity.

All three baseline probabilities in (2) are positive and differentiable in \(u\).  The mean-value theorem applied to their square roots therefore gives a constant \(C_0\), depending only on the fixed moment slack, such that the one-donor squared Hellinger distance is at most \(C_0\delta_N^2\).  Hellinger affinity multiplies under products.  Moreover, if \(p,q\) are densities and \(A=\int\sqrt{pq}\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \frac12\int|p-q|
 \le\frac12\{(2-2A)(2+2A)\}^{1/2}
 =(1-A^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.
\tag{6}
\]
Choosing the fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most \(1-\eta_0\) for some \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common independent uniform training design.  If \(0<\kappa<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), set \(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\).  Set the other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).  Choosing fixed positive \(b_0,b_1\) sufficiently small in terms of \(B,L\) puts every surface in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), keeps its values strictly inside \([-B,B]\), and gives
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.
\tag{7}
\]
Take identical bounded centered response noise in the two laws, so that \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})+\varepsilon_{sti}\), and take identical positive constant treated observations.  Set \(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and choose the unobserved \(B_{si}(0)\) to be the positive constant \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  With amplitudes small enough, all wealth levels lie in \((0,B)\).  To realize them as buy-and-hold levels in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, set \(W_{si,-1}=1\), \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\).  The defining product then equals \(B_{si}(a)\).  Independence makes the calendar sequence i.i.d., gives cross-unit independence and donor--training separation, and verifies both design-conditional centering equalities.  Consistency and event-date transport hold by construction.

The complete training and treated-event observed laws are identical under the two alternatives.  By \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (7), their targets differ by
\[
 \pi_1b_1\delta_N^\kappa
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (6) and (8) proves the claim without any lower local-modulus restriction.
